title: Bounded concurrency and back pressure decision
text: The architecture forum approves bounded concurrency, back pressure, circuit breaking, and retry budgets for MerchantConnect. Doubling the outbound connection pool alone is rejected as the durable solution because it does not bound retry amplification.

title: Bounded concurrency and back pressure decision
text: Admission must stop adding work when the downstream budget is exhausted. Circuit state must suppress calls to an unhealthy dependency, and retries must consume an explicit budget. The design preserves correlation identifiers so operators can follow one request through every attempted delivery.

title: Bounded concurrency and back pressure decision
text: Acceptance of the design is separate from deployment and change approval. A larger pool may be a temporary mitigation under the applicable control process, but is not the architecture decision recorded here.

title: Bounded concurrency and back pressure decision
text: Merchant payment processing crosses an outbound provider boundary. Waiting work, active connections, and client-visible responses describe different parts of that journey. A useful investigation preserves those distinctions and relates observations to the particular configuration and procedure in force. A temporary reduction in waiting work can be operationally useful without explaining why the original pressure accumulated. Service identity and observation time therefore remain essential when comparing records that use similar words for different failure modes.

title: Replay safe payments decision
text: The payment architecture forum mandates merchant-scoped idempotency keys and replay-safe settlement. A repeated request with the same merchant and key must resolve against the recorded operation rather than initiate an independent debit.

title: Replay safe payments decision
text: The key is bound to the normalized request payload. Reuse with a different payload must fail explicitly; ambiguous settlement acknowledgements must be reconciled before another submission. Persistence of the result must survive a worker restart so retries cannot bypass the boundary.

title: Replay safe payments decision
text: This decision specifies the target behavior. Evidence that a release was deployed belongs in the change record; evidence of the version running today requires the deployment system.

title: Replay safe payments decision
text: A payment operation can produce several network attempts. The commercial instruction, the transport attempt, and the settlement entry must remain distinguishable throughout investigation. An interrupted acknowledgement leaves uncertainty about the operation's result; it does not establish that repeating the request is harmless. Interface contracts and persistence boundaries determine what a retry means. Evidence should connect these boundaries through stable references before an analyst classifies an apparent duplicate or recommends further processing.

title: Replay safe payments decision
text: For example, a worker can submit a payment and lose the acknowledgement before returning a response to the merchant. The next worker must consult the same operation record before deciding what to do. It must not infer that the first submission failed merely because the first worker is no longer available. If the settlement outcome remains ambiguous, reconciliation is part of completing the operation, rather than a reason to create a second independent instruction.

title: Event consumer backpressure decision
text: The messaging architecture decision adopts bounded event consumption with explicit backlog management. Settlement consumers must report event age and committed position rather than presenting a running process as proof that processing has caught up.

title: Event consumer backpressure decision
text: Recovery prioritizes safe acknowledgement and reconciliation of outstanding work. Operators may adjust permitted consumer capacity only while preserving event ordering and downstream limits; blind replay is rejected because it can duplicate business processing.

title: Event consumer backpressure decision
text: The decision addresses backlog recovery, not a posting-order race inside the ledger. Deployment evidence and incident-specific recovery measurements remain separate records.

title: Event consumer backpressure decision
text: Settlement and reporting follow payment acceptance through asynchronous processing stages. Each stage can complete at a different time, and a report can be accurate for its stated cutoff while omitting more recent work. Investigation therefore follows source identifiers through event consumption, reconciliation, and publication. Delay, mismatch, and accounting correction are separate observations. Combining them under a single label without tracing their respective records can conceal both the actual processing bottleneck and the required control response.

title: Event consumer backpressure decision

That observation should trigger a check of where acknowledgement occurs and which work is still outstanding. It should not be interpreted as permission to raise the consumption limit indefinitely. The operator needs a view of event age and downstream completion for the same processing interval, with the original event references retained through any permitted retry or replay.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
Record what the checkout response actually establishes. Acceptance means the request entered processing; completion requires a business outcome. Preserve the support reference when an acknowledgement is interrupted so later investigation can distinguish a pending instruction from a fresh submission.

Related authority: [PROD-001 — PayFlow checkout journey](DOC-PROD-001.md#section-01), version 1, published 2025-07-18. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
Separate waiting work from active PSP sessions. An increase in acquisition waits can occur while inbound workers remain healthy. Capture the effective connection setting with the observation rather than inferring it from a queue graph or a remembered baseline.

Related authority: [ARCH-007 — MerchantConnect capacity configuration](DOC-ARCH-007.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-06-19. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
Compare attempts per original request with active connections and waiting work. Repeated attempts can intensify the same pressure that produced the original timeout. Increasing a resource limit without examining this feedback path can move the bottleneck to another dependency.

Related authority: [ARCHREV-004 — MerchantConnect retry amplification review](DOC-ARCHREV-004.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-06-25. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
Admission control decides whether additional work can enter the constrained path. Inspect what happens to deferred or rejected requests as well as accepted traffic. A smaller internal queue is not necessarily recovery if work disappeared without an attributable customer outcome.

Related authority: [ADR-021 — Bounded concurrency and back pressure decision](DOC-ADR-021.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-07-02. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
Follow pressure signals from the outbound boundary to the caller. Confirm that upstream work observes the signal instead of immediately retrying. Retain request identifiers across deferral so a bounded queue does not become a source of ambiguous payment outcomes.

Related authority: [RB-003-v2 — MerchantConnect revised saturation response](DOC-RB-003-v2.md#section-01), version 2, published 2026-07-16. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
A circuit protects an unhealthy dependency by suppressing calls under the accepted design. Investigate why it opened and what evidence permits another attempt. Treat circuit behavior and provider recovery as separate observations; an open circuit is not itself the provider's root cause.

Related authority: [ADR-021 — Bounded concurrency and back pressure decision](DOC-ADR-021.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-07-02. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
Check whether repeated attempts consume a bounded allowance associated with the operation. Worker movement must not silently reset the budget. Preserve the original key and outcome reference so a client cannot create apparently fresh work merely by changing transport details.

Related authority: [PROD-007 — Merchant retry guidance](DOC-PROD-007.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-07-31. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
A tuning release can improve waiting behavior without removing the underlying feedback mechanism. Preserve its actual configuration scope when comparing later events. Do not describe every temporary adjustment as the subsequent architectural redesign or assume that a completed change closed all recurrence actions.

Related authority: [CHG-139 — MerchantConnect pool tuning](DOC-CHG-139.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-03-28. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
Compute the proposed increase against the documented baseline and consult the effective approval rule. Record downstream assumptions and rollback conditions. The existence of spare local resources does not establish that the external provider can safely absorb more simultaneous requests.

Related authority: [POL-007-v2 — Material capacity change standard](DOC-POL-007-v2.md#section-01), version 2, published 2026-06-01. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
Keep the incident qualification, requested action, authority, implementation time, and recovery evidence distinguishable. A clear packet allows reviewers to assess urgency and compliance independently. Contacting the responsible person is only a communication step; retain the actual approval decision separately.

Related authority: [RB-010 — Emergency capacity change procedure](DOC-RB-010.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-06-03. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
Associate a retry with the merchant's business operation rather than the process that happened to send it. Preserve the key through interrupted acknowledgements. A replacement worker must find the persisted outcome instead of treating its first local observation as a new payment.

Related authority: [PROD-006-v2 — Merchant retry API current spec](DOC-PROD-006-v2.md#section-01), version 2, published 2026-07-30. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
Compare the normalized payload when a key already exists. A different amount or destination must not inherit a previous successful result or silently start a new debit. Retain the explicit conflict outcome so support can explain why the request was rejected.

Related authority: [ADR-024 — Replay safe payments decision](DOC-ADR-024.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-07-28. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
Trace uniqueness through settlement submission, not only the merchant-facing endpoint. An interface-level deduplication check is incomplete if another worker can independently submit the same business operation downstream. Retain the settlement reference beside the operation result for reconciliation.

Related authority: [ADR-024 — Replay safe payments decision](DOC-ADR-024.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-07-28. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
An interrupted acknowledgement leaves an uncertainty to resolve. Check persisted payment and settlement outcomes before replay. Generating a new key to escape the uncertainty can create a second business instruction and should not be described as ordinary transport recovery.

Related authority: [RB-004 — Duplicate payment triage](DOC-RB-004.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-07-30. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
Maintain separate counts for transport attempts, commercial instructions, and executed debits. A failed-attempt metric can include rejected work and repeated attempts. It therefore cannot be relabeled as a count of duplicate debits without examining the business-level evidence.

Related authority: [ARCHREV-006 — Duplicate debit boundary review](DOC-ARCHREV-006.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-07-24. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
When investigating an older client, identify the contract effective for that client and event date. Do not silently apply a later mandatory-key promise to an earlier interface. Versioned specifications explain what behavior was expected at each point in the history.

Related authority: [PROD-006-v1 — Merchant retry API prior spec](DOC-PROD-006-v1.md#section-01), version 1, published 2025-07-18. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
A deployment timestamp is a useful investigation boundary, but temporal proximity is not sufficient causal evidence. Compare the changed path with the incident's observed mechanism. Preserve release chronology even when a later review supplies a more complete explanation.

Related authority: [CHG-118 — Retry redesign release](DOC-CHG-118.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-07-19. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
Retain later retry events with their individual mechanisms. A family label is useful for discovery but too broad to establish recurrence of one defect. Compare operation identity, persisted outcomes, and affected boundaries before deciding that a fix failed.

Related authority: [ARCHREV-014 — Idempotency follow up review](DOC-ARCHREV-014.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-08-28. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
Payment acceptance and settlement consumption cross an asynchronous boundary. Track the producer reference and consumer position independently. A successful synchronous response can coexist with downstream delay without either observation being false.

Related authority: [ARCH-002 — Digital payment dependency map](DOC-ARCH-002.md#section-01), version 1, published 2025-07-15. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
Measure the age of unprocessed events as well as the number waiting. A queue can shrink because work moved, expired, or was discarded. Recovery evidence should show processing and acknowledgement, not only a lower count in a dashboard.

Related authority: [RB-008-v2 — EventMesh revised backlog response](DOC-RB-008-v2.md#section-01), version 2, published 2026-06-02. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
Inspect the delayed subscription or partition rather than relying only on process availability. A running consumer group may conceal one stalled path. Record the last committed position with the observation time so another responder can verify actual progress.

Related authority: [RB-005 — Settlement lag response](DOC-RB-005.md#section-01), version 1, published 2025-07-25. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
A recovery burst can overwhelm the next service even if the event consumer has spare capacity. Pace catch-up against downstream processing limits and preserve ordering. Reconciliation must confirm that accelerated consumption did not create a new ambiguity.

Related authority: [ADR-025 — Event consumer backpressure decision](DOC-ADR-025.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-05-28. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
A reconciliation result describes work completed through a specified cutoff. Retain outstanding references beyond that boundary and explain their disposition separately. Do not advance the cutoff solely because an upstream producer has resumed normal operation.

Related authority: [POL-012 — Settlement reconciliation standard](DOC-POL-012.md#section-01), version 1, published 2025-07-01. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
Explain the difference between report publication and the latest payment included. A newly opened report can still reflect an earlier processing cutoff. Customer support should preserve the report reference and cutoff when investigating missing recent activity.

Related authority: [PROD-009 — Corporate reconciliation report spec](DOC-PROD-009.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-05-25. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
Use the existence of a ledger-control reference as a reason to seek authorized evidence, not to infer its contents. Event backlog and posting order are different investigative paths. An operations handbook must not reproduce confidential accounting-adjustment evidence for an unauthorized reader.

Related authority: [ARCHREV-008 — EventMesh settlement dependency review](DOC-ARCHREV-008.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-05-22. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
A database acquisition wait and an outbound HTTP pool wait can share a symptom while requiring different checks. Identify the resource and owning service before applying a runbook. Preserve original error codes alongside any plain-language summary.

Related authority: [ARCH-006 — Payment error taxonomy](DOC-ARCH-006.md#section-01), version 1, published 2025-07-20. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
A reset identifies an interrupted connection boundary. It does not by itself show that local sessions were exhausted or that the provider's internal cause is known. Retain the connection phase and request outcome uncertainty during classification.

Related authority: [ARCH-006 — Payment error taxonomy](DOC-ARCH-006.md#section-01), version 1, published 2025-07-20. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
Resolution occurs before a new outbound session can be established. Confirm whether the endpoint was resolved before attributing failure to pool capacity. Existing healthy sessions may coexist with failures to create new ones when resolution is impaired.

Related authority: [ARCH-006 — Payment error taxonomy](DOC-ARCH-006.md#section-01), version 1, published 2025-07-20. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
Certificate validation failure is different from an unavailable connection slot. Record the trust error and connection stage without disabling validation as an assumed remedy. The incident's approved recovery evidence, rather than the shared word timeout, determines classification.

Related authority: [ARCH-006 — Payment error taxonomy](DOC-ARCH-006.md#section-01), version 1, published 2025-07-20. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
Assign the incident to the service whose interruption is recorded. A downstream dependency named in its explanation does not automatically create a second incident. Preserve cross-service consequences without duplicating the same event in a collection analysis.

Related authority: [ARCH-002 — Digital payment dependency map](DOC-ARCH-002.md#section-01), version 1, published 2025-07-15. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
Use the incident identifier to reconcile a report, change reference, and compendium entry. Multiple documents can describe one event. Keep separate source citations while preserving one event identity for any later calculation over incident records.

Related authority: [ARCH-006 — Payment error taxonomy](DOC-ARCH-006.md#section-01), version 1, published 2025-07-20. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
Read the start and end of the attributable interruption rather than substituting ticket-open time. The reporting purpose determines whether recovery observation or administrative closure matters. An unresolved financial item can remain after an operational interruption ends.

Related authority: [POL-012 — Settlement reconciliation standard](DOC-POL-012.md#section-01), version 1, published 2025-07-01. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
A failed attempt does not identify a unique customer. Repeated attempts and shared corporate operators can make those units diverge substantially. Preserve unknown customer counts explicitly and avoid translating attempt totals into customer totals without additional evidence.

Related authority: [PROD-005 — Settlement report delivery contract](DOC-PROD-005.md#section-01), version 1, published 2025-07-18. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
Delayed reporting and failed attempts can create concern without establishing a measured loss. A monetary assessment needs its own recorded amounts and methodology. Do not introduce an assumed average payment value to make an incomplete operational metric appear financially precise.

Related authority: [PROD-009 — Corporate reconciliation report spec](DOC-PROD-009.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-05-25. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
State the periods being compared and retain qualifying residual incidents. Unequal exposure windows and missing traffic denominators limit the interpretation of a before-and-after comparison. The reports support observation; they do not independently supply a controlled causal experiment.

Related authority: [ARCHREV-013 — Post rollout capacity load review](DOC-ARCHREV-013.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-08-28. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
Publication, effective date, and event date answer different questions. A policy may be published before it takes effect, while a report may be written after the event. Select the rule applicable to the action rather than simply the newest file.

Related authority: [POL-007-v2 — Material capacity change standard](DOC-POL-007-v2.md#section-01), version 2, published 2026-06-01. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
Historical documents explain completed events and procedures. A present incident enquiry needs a current operational record with an update time. If that record is unavailable, preserve uncertainty instead of substituting a recent release note as a status report.

Related authority: [RB-009 — Payment live triage](DOC-RB-009.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-08-20. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
Resolve whether the request concerns an owner, incident commander, manager, or shift responder. Those roles can be held by different people. Use the appropriate dated or current authority before requesting contact details, and retain the service identifier through the lookup.

Related authority: [RB-013 — Service ownership escalation guide](DOC-RB-013.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-07-02. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
Support should distinguish pending confirmation from confirmed failure or completion. A transport error alone may leave the business result unresolved. Preserve the original support reference so the customer is not encouraged to submit duplicate instructions to discover the outcome.

Related authority: [PROD-001 — PayFlow checkout journey](DOC-PROD-001.md#section-01), version 1, published 2025-07-18. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Payments Architecture and Operations Handbook
text:
Transfer observed symptoms, attempted actions, preserved references, and unresolved hypotheses together. The next responder should know which boundary was checked and which remains uncertain. A handover that only says fixed or still broken loses the evidence needed to continue investigation.

Related authority: [RB-003-v2 — MerchantConnect revised saturation response](DOC-RB-003-v2.md#section-01), version 2, published 2026-07-16. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
Begin a control review by naming the decision being assessed and its effective period. A policy recommendation, approved rule, and implemented setting are different records. Preserve their sequence so a reviewer can see whether the required authority existed when the action occurred.

Related authority: [POL-019 — Corporate limit review cadence](DOC-POL-019.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-03-27. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
A segment-based allowance depends on verified eligibility. Retain the evidence establishing that status and distinguish it from a customer's desire for a higher limit. Product demand can motivate a review without supplying the eligibility evidence needed for a particular customer.

Related authority: [RISK-003 — Corporate limit regulatory review](DOC-RISK-003.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-03-10. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
Examine whether usage is shared across operators and channels for the corporate customer. Testing only a single user can miss a bypass at the account boundary. Preserve the accounting interval and policy version alongside the resulting limit decision.

Related authority: [ARCH-003 — Corporate limit enforcement design](DOC-ARCH-003.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-03-25. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
Read conditional approval together with its outstanding requirements. A committee's support for a proposal does not mean every prerequisite has been satisfied. Track the policy and implementation records that convert the decision into an operative customer rule.

Related authority: [MTG-003 — Corporate limit risk committee](DOC-MTG-003.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-03-20. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
Retain the prior version and the replacement's effective boundary. Historical decisions need the version in force at the time. A present search result should not erase evidence that a different allowance legitimately applied earlier.

Related authority: [POL-002-v2 — Corporate daily limit effective policy](DOC-POL-002-v2.md#section-01), version 2, published 2026-03-26. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
Distinguish record correction from a request to depart from policy. Correcting a mistaken customer segment does not grant unrestricted discretion to increase an allowance. Any exception requires attributable authority and a scope that can be examined later.

Related authority: [RB-006 — Corporate limit support procedure](DOC-RB-006.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-03-28. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
Compare web and API treatment of the same corporate customer and accounting interval. A channel change must not reset consumption or verification state. Differences in wording should not create contradictory explanations of the governing rule.

Related authority: [PROD-012 — Corporate channel limit matrix](DOC-PROD-012.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-03-30. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
A scheduled review is an opportunity to assess whether the rule remains appropriate. It is not an automatic permission to change it. Retain the evidence considered, recommendation, authorized disposition, and effective replacement where one is approved.

Related authority: [POL-019 — Corporate limit review cadence](DOC-POL-019.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-03-27. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
Preserve the model release and comparable decision sample before evaluating an adjustment. Changes in cohort composition can affect observed complaints independently of model behavior. Review conclusions should identify the comparison population and its limitations.

Related authority: [RISK-001 — Fraud false positive analysis](DOC-RISK-001.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-04-28. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
Authorized feature investigation serves a different audience from customer support. Retain extraction time and decision context within the permitted evidence boundary. Do not make detailed feature descriptions available by copying them into a broadly accessible summary.

Related authority: [RISK-002 — Fraud feature investigation](DOC-RISK-002.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-04-29. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
A complaint is a signal for examination, not automatically a confirmed false positive. Link it to the reviewed disposition before drawing conclusions. Keep unknown outcomes visible so unresolved complaints do not become fabricated favorable results.

Related authority: [RISK-001 — Fraud false positive analysis](DOC-RISK-001.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-04-28. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
A threshold adjustment can transfer work into manual review. Assess queue behavior and review capacity alongside customer friction. A decrease in automated rejection does not establish improvement if unresolved review work simply accumulates elsewhere.

Related authority: [MTG-005 — Fraud model committee](DOC-MTG-005.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-05-04. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
Evaluate the possibility of additional fraud exposure even when customer friction falls. The available operational evidence may not quantify a monetary effect. Record that limitation instead of converting a directional tradeoff into an unsupported financial claim.

Related authority: [POL-010-v2 — Fraud model governance current policy](DOC-POL-010-v2.md#section-01), version 2, published 2026-05-01. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
Identify the exact adjustment and observation obligations accepted by the committee. Approval for one bounded change is not standing authority for further tuning. Preserve the rollback condition and responsible review owner with the release packet.

Related authority: [MTG-005 — Fraud model committee](DOC-MTG-005.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-05-04. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
A model release and a threshold configuration are distinct changes. Retain both references when examining a decision. Without that separation, an investigator may attribute behavior to the wrong modification or overlook a cohort-mapping issue.

Related authority: [CHG-109 — Fraud model threshold release](DOC-CHG-109.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-05-10. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
A rollback still changes a control and requires the applicable authority. Capture the trigger and pre-action evidence before implementation. Returning to an earlier setting does not remove the need to verify customer and review-queue behavior afterward.

Related authority: [RB-007 — Fraud threshold rollback](DOC-RB-007.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-05-06. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
Customer wording should explain the permitted next step and preserve a support reference. It should not reveal the rule features or imply that a customer can obtain approval by repeating a pattern. Pending review must remain distinguishable from final rejection.

Related authority: [PROD-011 — Sanitized decline messaging](DOC-PROD-011.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-05-12. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
Define the unit behind any claimed benefit. Failed attempts, customers, transactions, and currency amounts are not interchangeable. If monetary loss was not measured, retain the unknown rather than introduce an average-value assumption to complete a business case.

Related authority: [RISK-005 — Settlement delay impact review](DOC-RISK-005.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-05-26. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
Evaluate the requested increase against the effective capacity rule and documented baseline. Retain the calculation in the approval packet. A proposed doubling and a small adjustment can share an operational aim while falling into different governance paths.

Related authority: [POL-007-v2 — Material capacity change standard](DOC-POL-007-v2.md#section-01), version 2, published 2026-06-01. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
The expedited route depends on the qualifying incident and applicable policy. Keep the evidence establishing urgency separate from the proposed technical action. A responder's assertion that a change is urgent does not replace the recorded incident qualification.

Related authority: [RB-010 — Emergency capacity change procedure](DOC-RB-010.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-06-03. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
Identify the approval decision that existed before implementation under the permitted path. A directory result helps find a responsible person but does not prove they approved the action. Preserve decision time and scope rather than only a name.

Related authority: [POL-007-v2 — Material capacity change standard](DOC-POL-007-v2.md#section-01), version 2, published 2026-06-01. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
Start the review interval from implementation, not ticket completion. Record the implementation and approval timestamps as independent fields. A late explanatory note can improve the record without changing whether the original deadline was met.

Related authority: [POL-011 — Emergency change review standard](DOC-POL-011.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-06-02. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
A change can restore service and still leave a governance obligation unmet. Preserve the observed technical result rather than changing it to match the compliance verdict. Reviewers need both timelines to explain the case accurately.

Related authority: [CHG-160 — Emergency pool mitigation](DOC-CHG-160.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-08-10. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
Assess timeliness against the evidence available at the required boundary. A later approval cannot be represented as timely simply because the incident was resolved. Keep the exception visible and assign a corrective process action.

Related authority: [RISK-007 — Emergency change control finding](DOC-RISK-007.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-08-12. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
Follow-up actions should address why the deadline or evidence requirement was missed. Rewriting the original timestamps is not remediation. Retain the operational result, the control finding, and the proposed prevention mechanism as distinct parts of the record.

Related authority: [MTG-011 — Emergency change review](DOC-MTG-011.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-08-13. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
An audit finding must describe the gap and the evidence that made it observable. Avoid replacing a missing disposition with a presumption of approval. The remediation plan should address the identified gap rather than merely produce a new tool or screen.

Related authority: [RISK-008 — Privileged access audit finding](DOC-RISK-008.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-05-05. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
A review cannot establish coverage without the population assigned to the cycle. Retain that population with subsequent decisions and exceptions. Otherwise, a list of completed reviews may conceal access items that were never examined.

Related authority: [RB-011 — Privileged review evidence procedure](DOC-RB-011.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-05-21. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
A scheduled monthly process needs evidence of actual completion for each cycle. Assignment and reminder records demonstrate workflow activity, not the final disposition. Unanswered items must remain distinguishable from reviewed and approved access.

Related authority: [POL-013-v2 — Privileged review revised policy](DOC-POL-013-v2.md#section-01), version 2, published 2026-05-20. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
A workflow release establishes that a mechanism was delivered. It does not establish that reviewers used it correctly in later cycles. Preserve release checks and operating evidence separately so assurance can follow the complete chain.

Related authority: [CHG-167 — Privileged review workflow release](DOC-CHG-167.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-05-25. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
An exception must retain its reason, responsible owner, and current evidence of disposition. Closing the surrounding review does not automatically resolve every exception. Keep pending removals separate from access changes that have actually completed.

Related authority: [RB-011 — Privileged review evidence procedure](DOC-RB-011.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-05-21. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
Verification follows implementation and examination of completed operating cycles. The verifier should be able to trace the population, decisions, and resulting changes. Independence matters because an implementation owner's completion statement alone cannot establish sustained operation.

Related authority: [RISK-009 — Independent closure verification](DOC-RISK-009.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-08-18. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
Closure applies to the finding and verification period actually examined. It does not certify every privileged system indefinitely. Retain the original scope and ongoing obligations so later readers do not interpret closure as a permanent waiver.

Related authority: [MTG-012 — Audit closure committee](DOC-MTG-012.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-08-20. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
Sensitive control configuration has a narrower audience than general review obligations. A review summary should identify the applicable evidence without reproducing privileged implementation details. Source access boundaries remain relevant when information is combined into a manual.

Related authority: [POL-013-v2 — Privileged review revised policy](DOC-POL-013-v2.md#section-01), version 2, published 2026-05-20. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
Keep accepted instructions, consumed events, and reconciled entries distinguishable. An unmatched item requires a supported disposition. A report that is delayed or incomplete should state its cutoff instead of implying that all current activity has been reconciled.

Related authority: [POL-012 — Settlement reconciliation standard](DOC-POL-012.md#section-01), version 1, published 2025-07-01. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
A manual adjustment requires its own rationale and review evidence. A balanced result after correction does not establish that the original control operated properly. Link the accounting outcome to the incident without merging unrelated event-backlog and posting-order mechanisms.

Related authority: [RISK-006 — Ledger posting race control finding](DOC-RISK-006.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-06-29. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
Assess completeness relative to the reported cutoff and outstanding work. Publication time alone is insufficient. Customer communication should explain what is represented and what remains unresolved without inventing a financial loss from delayed visibility.

Related authority: [RISK-005 — Settlement delay impact review](DOC-RISK-005.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-05-26. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
Define recovery in terms of the required customer journey and its dependencies. Successful infrastructure checks remain useful evidence even when a downstream checkpoint fails. Record partial recovery explicitly instead of averaging different outcomes into an overall success label.

Related authority: [POL-014 — DR dependency testing standard](DOC-POL-014.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-04-16. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
A controlled notification should traverse the same relevant boundaries as the exercised journey. Retain delivery and acknowledgement outcomes separately from database recovery. An untested notification path cannot inherit another component's successful result.

Related authority: [RB-012-v2 — DR failover revised procedure](DOC-RB-012-v2.md#section-01), version 2, published 2026-04-22. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
Use effective dates to assess accountability during a handover. Preserve original design attribution while tracking transferred operational duties. A later catalog entry cannot rewrite who was accountable under an earlier operating model.

Related authority: [POL-015 — Service ownership transfer policy](DOC-POL-015.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-06-22. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Operational Risk and Control Manual
text:
A review conclusion should state what was examined and what remains outside scope. Unknown measurements and missing records are limits on the answer, not opportunities to complete it from intuition. Preserve those limits when summarizing for a different audience.

Related authority: [RISK-009 — Independent closure verification](DOC-RISK-009.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-08-18. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
text: This compendium is a discovery aid for completed incident reports. Each entry preserves one incident identity and points to the primary report. Summaries are not additional incidents. Read the report's mechanism, measurement boundary, and references before classifying an event or comparing it with another service.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
text: The entries cover the historical reports available through August 2026. Payment and adjacent-service events are identified separately in the primary reports. A question about a different population needs its own inclusion criteria; shared vocabulary or a dependency reference does not automatically place an event in that population.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
text: Interruption minutes, failed attempts, unique payments, customers, and currency loss are different units. Preserve the definition recorded in each primary report. Unrecorded measurements remain unknown. A compilation of references does not supply a missing denominator, a duplicate-debit count, or a monetary loss estimate.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
text: Completed reports describe their own events. They do not supply present incident status, current ownership, active employee details, or an on-call assignment. A present enquiry needs the appropriate current operational record and its observation time. Similar historical symptoms are a basis for investigation, not a confirmed live cause.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
text:
Outbound pool exhausted when a burst of merchant requests occupied PSP sessions faster than they were released; MC_POOL_WAIT accompanied rising acquisition waits.

The failure involved outbound provider capacity rather than a database pool. This report does not establish a general policy for increasing the configured ceiling.

Primary evidence: [INC-2025-006](DOC-INC-2025-006.md#section-02), published 2025-08-20. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
section_heading: PSP Gateway external provider degradation — INC-2025-008
text:
The PSP Gateway received provider-side connection resets, recorded as PSP_CONN_RESET. The upstream session was closed before a complete response reached the gateway.

A connection reset is not the same as local pool exhaustion. The external dependency interruption explains this event without establishing the provider's internal root cause.

Primary evidence: [INC-2025-008](DOC-INC-2025-008.md#section-02), published 2025-09-02. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
text:
A PayFlow retry worker lost a lease acknowledgement and scheduled an already-pending status attempt again. Repeated retries consumed the operation's permitted attempt budget.

The reviewed defect is in retry scheduling. The event does not record executed duplicate debits or evidence that a merchant idempotency boundary was absent.

Primary evidence: [INC-2025-009](DOC-INC-2025-009.md#section-02), published 2025-09-06. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
text:
PayFlow database connection-pool waits grew behind long-running transaction locks. PF_DB_POOL_WAIT identified the database acquisition boundary rather than the outbound PSP client pool.

The word pool is a lexical similarity to MerchantConnect incidents, but the constrained resource and root-cause family are different.

Primary evidence: [INC-2025-011](DOC-INC-2025-011.md#section-02), published 2025-09-26. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
text:
SettlementHub consumer lag accumulated behind an EventMesh event burst. Accepted payment work reached downstream reconciliation later than expected.

A payment's acceptance time and appearance in a report are different milestones. This event does not establish a ledger posting-order defect.

Primary evidence: [INC-2025-012](DOC-INC-2025-012.md#section-02), published 2025-10-03. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
text:
PSP sessions were consumed by excess worker fan-out introduced in a concurrency configuration deployment. The resulting capacity pressure outlasted individual client timeouts.

The preceding change is part of the confirmed event sequence. A timeout still did not establish whether every affected business instruction had failed permanently.

Primary evidence: [INC-2025-014](DOC-INC-2025-014.md#section-02), published 2025-11-04. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
text:
MerchantConnect resolver timeouts prevented establishment of new PSP connections. Existing sessions and worker capacity did not remove the need to resolve the upstream endpoint.

This is a MerchantConnect DNS event, not an outbound-capacity event. Counting it with pool starvation would conflate failure to locate an endpoint with lack of available sessions.

Primary evidence: [INC-2025-018](DOC-INC-2025-018.md#section-02), published 2025-11-18. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
text:
A MerchantConnect deployment reset retry counters when work moved between workers. Operations consequently exceeded the intended retry allowance and received downstream rejections.

This retry-budget defect is separate from the later missing-key payment boundary. Shared family membership is not proof of an identical cause.

Primary evidence: [INC-2025-021](DOC-INC-2025-021.md#section-02), published 2025-12-03. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
text:
An external PSP accepted connections but responded slowly enough that MerchantConnect requests exceeded their processing window. The provider degradation persisted after local worker availability was confirmed.

Although MerchantConnect was affected, the confirmed family is external PSP degradation. Counting every merchant timeout as local capacity exhaustion would misclassify the event.

Primary evidence: [INC-2025-026](DOC-INC-2025-026.md#section-02), published 2025-12-17. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
section_heading: MerchantConnect configuration and trust interruption — INC-2025-031
text:
MerchantConnect trust configuration rejected the provider certificate chain during connection establishment. TLS_TRUST_FAILURE was retained with affected request references.

This is a certificate or configuration event. It does not imply that the fictional provider's certificate was malicious or that a local capacity change was warranted.

Primary evidence: [INC-2025-031](DOC-INC-2025-031.md#section-02), published 2025-12-30. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
section_heading: AuthHub configuration and trust interruption — INC-2025-034
text:
An expired AuthHub certificate interrupted authentication. AUTH_TLS_EXPIRED identified the certificate boundary and an alert-routing gap delayed recognition by the responsible responder.

The event concerns authentication infrastructure. Its impact belongs to the identity service and cannot establish present certificate or employee status.

Primary evidence: [INC-2025-034](DOC-INC-2025-034.md#section-02), published 2026-01-01. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
text:
AuthHub HTTP client pool starvation affected identity lookups. AUTH_HTTP_POOL_WAIT used wording similar to payment connection failures but referred to the authentication client boundary.

This event concerns the identity lookup boundary. Shared pool terminology does not make it an interruption of the merchant payment service.

Primary evidence: [INC-2026-006](DOC-INC-2026-006.md#section-02), published 2026-01-15. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
text:
MerchantConnect client pool starvation was amplified by retries after a worker retry-timing deployment. Retried attempts competed with original calls for the same outbound sessions.

The root-cause family is capacity because exhaustion of outbound sessions interrupted service. The presence of retries does not make this a duplicate-debit incident.

Primary evidence: [INC-2026-011](DOC-INC-2026-011.md#section-02), published 2026-01-22. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
text:
A PayFlow retry-jitter deployment synchronized delayed attempts instead of dispersing them. Concentrated retry traffic caused requests to exhaust their permitted processing window.

The event records failed or rejected attempts, not a count of unique customers. It does not quantify the monetary effect of those attempts.

Primary evidence: [INC-2026-013](DOC-INC-2026-013.md#section-02), published 2026-02-03. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
section_heading: PSP Gateway external provider degradation — INC-2026-016
text:
The PSP Gateway experienced prolonged upstream response unavailability. Local request handling remained available, but the external authorization path did not provide usable responses.

The report establishes an external service interruption as observed by Northstar. It does not speculate about an unobserved internal failure at the fictional provider.

Primary evidence: [INC-2026-016](DOC-INC-2026-016.md#section-02), published 2026-02-13. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
text:
Slow PSP responses held MerchantConnect outbound connections while new merchant requests continued to arrive. Acquisition waits increased until callers observed timeouts.

This event concerned capacity held by slow responses, not an observed provider connection reset. Similar client errors alone are insufficient to merge those mechanisms.

Primary evidence: [INC-2026-017](DOC-INC-2026-017.md#section-02), published 2026-02-20. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
text:
A stalled SettlementHub consumer partition left an increasing age of unprocessed events while other partitions continued. Aggregate process availability obscured the delayed subset.

A running consumer group alone would have overstated recovery. The report concerns event backlog, not a confirmed financial loss from delayed reporting.

Primary evidence: [INC-2026-019](DOC-INC-2026-019.md#section-02), published 2026-03-03. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
text:
A SettlementHub database-index deployment increased lock contention during reconciliation writes. The resulting database waits delayed processing of otherwise available settlement work.

The event is database contention associated with a change. It must not be relabeled as EventMesh backlog solely because settlement completion was delayed.

Primary evidence: [INC-2026-022](DOC-INC-2026-022.md#section-02), published 2026-03-20. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
text:
MerchantConnect outbound pool exhaustion recurred as requests continued entering a saturated downstream path. Waiting work triggered further attempts and prolonged pressure on the client pool.

Restoration of the queue did not demonstrate removal of the feedback loop. Follow-up remediation required its own implementation and operating evidence.

Primary evidence: [INC-2026-024](DOC-INC-2026-024.md#section-02), published 2026-03-27. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
text:
A regional DR exercise restored the database but left NotifyHub unavailable through the exercised recovery path. The exercise inventory had omitted the notification dependency.

The duration measures the exercise's attributable notification interruption. It is not a current regional-health observation or a payment-outage interval.

Primary evidence: [INC-2026-025](DOC-INC-2026-025.md#section-02), published 2026-04-06. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
text:
A campaign spike reached SettlementHub after a consumer configuration change had reduced effective processing capacity. EventMesh lag delayed settlement consumption and reconciliation.

The observed backlog supports a change-related event. Its effect on corporate reporting requires the downstream product and architecture evidence rather than an assumed universal customer impact.

Primary evidence: [INC-2026-029](DOC-INC-2026-029.md#section-02), published 2026-05-19. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
section_heading: FraudShield configuration and trust interruption — INC-2026-030
text:
A cohort-mapping configuration defect after MODEL-2026-04 caused inappropriate review routing and a customer-visible false-positive spike. The incident captures a specific operational symptom within the broader model-governance story.

This configuration event does not establish a measured fraud loss or prove that the previously approved bounded threshold adjustment was never implemented.

Primary evidence: [INC-2026-030](DOC-INC-2026-030.md#section-02), published 2026-05-21. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
text:
MerchantConnect encountered intermittent upstream authorization errors during an external PSP degradation. Retrying the same operation did not reliably obtain a final response.

The event's duration is the attributable interruption interval. It is not a measurement of the provider's entire outage across all of its customers.

Primary evidence: [INC-2026-032](DOC-INC-2026-032.md#section-02), published 2026-05-30. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
section_heading: PSP Gateway network dependency interruption — INC-2026-033
text:
A PSP Gateway routing deployment directed authorization traffic through an unavailable network path. Requests failed before a usable provider response could return.

The change relation is supported by route evidence. It does not establish provider-side degradation or a failure of the idempotency contract.

Primary evidence: [INC-2026-033](DOC-INC-2026-033.md#section-02), published 2026-06-01. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
section_heading: PayFlow configuration and trust interruption — INC-2026-035
text:
A PayFlow deployment supplied an invalid timeout configuration to the outbound request path. Requests expired before the expected response interval could complete.

The failure belongs to configuration, despite timeout symptoms. It does not prove a repeated MerchantConnect capacity mechanism.

Primary evidence: [INC-2026-035](DOC-INC-2026-035.md#section-02), published 2026-06-09. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
text:
Unbounded concurrency and retry amplification starved MerchantConnect outbound sessions. MC_POOL_WAIT appeared with waiting requests even though inbound workers remained available.

The available event evidence supports a mechanism investigation. A later meeting proposal or architecture decision must not be treated as already approved at this report's publication.

Primary evidence: [INC-2026-038](DOC-INC-2026-038.md#section-02), published 2026-06-19. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
text:
A LedgerCore posting-order race produced inconsistent reconciliation order and required a manual accounting adjustment. The failure was inside the posting path rather than the EventMesh consumer boundary.

The event concerns the finance posting path. A broader payment analysis must state whether that path is in scope rather than silently treating every reconciliation event as a merchant payment interruption.

Primary evidence: [INC-2026-040](DOC-INC-2026-040.md#section-02), published 2026-06-26. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
text:
PayFlow hot-row contention serialized checkout state updates under concentrated access. Database waits increased while outbound payment capacity remained available.

The confirmed mechanism concerns local database serialization. A client timeout by itself would not distinguish this from an outbound provider problem.

Primary evidence: [INC-2026-041](DOC-INC-2026-041.md#section-02), published 2026-07-01. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
text:
Retries crossed the MerchantConnect payment boundary without a merchant-scoped idempotency key after the July retry redesign. Interrupted acknowledgements could trigger independent execution, and duplicate debits were observed.

The 44,700 failed or rejected attempts are not the number of duplicate debits. The report does not record an exact currency loss or establish that every retry-family event shares this mechanism.

Primary evidence: [INC-2026-043](DOC-INC-2026-043.md#section-02), published 2026-07-22. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
text:
A short merchant burst exhausted the bounded outbound allocation before back pressure stabilized admission. A minor capacity interruption remained visible after the July control rollout.

The event is retained as an observed residual failure. It does not establish that the rollout had no benefit, and it prevents a claim that capacity incidents were eliminated.

Primary evidence: [INC-2026-046](DOC-INC-2026-046.md#section-02), published 2026-07-24. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
text:
A concentrated settlement batch exceeded the bounded consumption path's short-term processing allowance. Event age increased until the batch could be reconciled.

A bounded recovery mechanism can coexist with a later backlog event. This report does not establish that the prior consumer change was absent or ineffective in every condition.

Primary evidence: [INC-2026-047](DOC-INC-2026-047.md#section-02), published 2026-07-31. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
text:
PayFlow checkout workers exhausted their outbound MerchantConnect allocation during a concentrated traffic burst. The constrained resource was the outbound request pool, not PayFlow's database connection pool.

This is a PayFlow capacity event. It should not be counted as a MerchantConnect-owned capacity incident merely because MerchantConnect was the downstream dependency.

Primary evidence: [INC-2026-049](DOC-INC-2026-049.md#section-02), published 2026-08-02. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
text:
DataGateway resolver timeouts interrupted its own upstream lookup path. DG_DNS_TIMEOUT described name resolution rather than occupied MerchantConnect PSP sessions.

This event is unrelated to MerchantConnect capacity recurrence. The existence of a dependency relationship is insufficient to assert that the same incident propagated into payments.

Primary evidence: [INC-2026-050](DOC-INC-2026-050.md#section-02), published 2026-08-03. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
text:
A PayFlow deployment changed retry classification so terminal declines re-entered the retry queue. Repeatedly attempting a terminal outcome consumed processing capacity and generated further rejections.

This is a retry classification defect, not evidence of missing merchant-scoped keys in MerchantConnect. A terminal decline must not be retried merely to seek a different answer.

Primary evidence: [INC-2026-051](DOC-INC-2026-051.md#section-02), published 2026-08-04. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
section_heading: PSP Gateway external provider degradation — INC-2026-052
text:
Provider-side throttling interrupted PSP Gateway authorization attempts. Local capacity was available, but upstream rejection prevented successful completion of the affected requests.

The report classifies observed external degradation. It does not infer that changing Northstar's local connection ceiling would have removed the provider's restriction.

Primary evidence: [INC-2026-052](DOC-INC-2026-052.md#section-02), published 2026-08-05. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: 2025 to 2026 Incident Review Compendium
text:
A MerchantConnect worker-lease deployment prematurely released retry ownership during acknowledgement reconciliation. Multiple workers attempted the same reconciliation task, producing rejected attempts and delayed resolution.

The reviewed defect concerns reconciliation ownership after the duplicate-prevention release. This report does not record renewed duplicate debits or universal failure of the idempotency fix.

Primary evidence: [INC-2026-054](DOC-INC-2026-054.md#section-02), published 2026-08-28. The primary report retains the attributable interval, impact units, response, and change assessment.

title: Digital Banking Platform Technical Reference
text:
Map the customer journey across synchronous requests and asynchronous work. Each boundary has its own acceptance and completion evidence. A successful response from one component does not establish that every downstream consumer or reporting stage has completed.

Related authority: [ARCH-002 — Digital payment dependency map](DOC-ARCH-002.md#section-01), version 1, published 2025-07-15. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Digital Banking Platform Technical Reference
text:
Retain the team named in the original dated design when discussing authorship. Operational responsibility can change later without making that historical attribution wrong. Do not replace it with a present catalog result unless the question explicitly concerns current ownership.

Related authority: [ARCH-001 — MerchantConnect original design](DOC-ARCH-001.md#section-01), version 1, published 2025-07-10. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Digital Banking Platform Technical Reference
text:
A handover transfers defined responsibilities rather than retroactively changing the design record. Check runbooks, unresolved actions, escalation duties, and catalog stewardship. These obligations may move together but still require distinct acceptance evidence.

Related authority: [ADR-027 — Service ownership operating model](DOC-ADR-027.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-06-15. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Digital Banking Platform Technical Reference
text:
Identify when the transfer takes effect rather than using the publication date of the minutes as a substitute. Questions about the transition boundary need the effective policy. Original design and later operation may therefore have different correct owners.

Related authority: [POL-015 — Service ownership transfer policy](DOC-POL-015.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-06-22. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Digital Banking Platform Technical Reference
text:
A dated migration explains why a catalog changed at that time. It does not provide a live roster indefinitely. Retain the source decision and migration reference so the historical transition can be reconstructed independently of later catalog edits.

Related authority: [CHG-172 — Ownership catalog migration](DOC-CHG-172.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-07-01. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Digital Banking Platform Technical Reference
text:
The designer of a component is not automatically its present responder. Resolve the requested responsibility before identifying a person. A historical architecture citation can answer who designed a service while remaining unsuitable for today's escalation contact.

Related authority: [RB-013 — Service ownership escalation guide](DOC-RB-013.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-07-02. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Digital Banking Platform Technical Reference
text:
An on-call assignment applies to a time interval. Preserve the requested time and service identity when seeking the responder. A name copied from an earlier incident cannot establish coverage for a later shift or an arbitrary historical date.

Related authority: [RB-009 — Payment live triage](DOC-RB-009.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-08-20. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Digital Banking Platform Technical Reference
text:
Incident coordination and technical shift coverage are different roles. Follow the incident record for command responsibility and the applicable roster for the responder. Do not collapse them merely because one person happened to perform both roles in an earlier event.

Related authority: [RB-009 — Payment live triage](DOC-RB-009.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-08-20. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Digital Banking Platform Technical Reference
text:
An inventory must follow customer-visible work beyond the primary database. Trace event delivery, consumption, notification preparation, and acknowledgement where they are required. An omitted dependency can make infrastructure restoration look more complete than the customer experience.

Related authority: [ADR-026 — DR dependency inventory decision](DOC-ADR-026.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-04-15. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Digital Banking Platform Technical Reference
text:
Database restoration demonstrates the checks that were actually performed. It does not establish that an omitted application dependency recovered. Preserve the old checklist when examining why an earlier exercise produced an incomplete result.

Related authority: [RB-012-v1 — DR failover prior procedure](DOC-RB-012-v1.md#section-01), version 1, published 2025-07-25. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Digital Banking Platform Technical Reference
text:
A notification journey has its own checkpoints after data is restored. Identify the path from event availability to acknowledged delivery. The ability to read restored records is a prerequisite observation, not proof that customers received the intended messages.

Related authority: [ARCHREV-012 — DR dependency gap review](DOC-ARCHREV-012.md#section-01), version 1, published 2026-04-10. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Digital Banking Platform Technical Reference
text:
Use the revised checklist for exercises after its effective boundary and retain the previous version for historical analysis. Each exercise still needs execution evidence. Publication of a better procedure does not retroactively make an earlier test pass.

Related authority: [RB-012-v2 — DR failover revised procedure](DOC-RB-012-v2.md#section-01), version 2, published 2026-04-22. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Digital Banking Platform Technical Reference
text:
Communicate which function was verified and which remains impaired. A precise partial result is more useful than a broad success label when the journey crosses several dependencies. Preserve the recovery reference so support can connect customer observations with the tested path.

Related authority: [PROD-010 — DR customer notification behavior](DOC-PROD-010.md#section-01), version 1, published 2025-07-18. Use the referenced record's effective interval and stated scope when applying this section.

title: Digital Banking Platform Technical Reference
text:
Keep exercise messages distinguishable from real customer traffic. Record the acknowledgement and test reference so the result can be verified without misleading customers. Adding a checkpoint is implementation work; passing a later exercise is operating evidence.

title: Corporate daily limit effective policy
text: Corporate payment eligibility, daily consumption, and operator permissions answer different questions. A customer can be eligible for an allowance while lacking enough remaining usage for a particular request. Equally, an authorized operator cannot change the corporate customer's segment simply by choosing another channel. Policy dates matter because a correct historical decision can differ from the rule applied later. Customer explanations must preserve the relevant segment, accounting interval, and effective version instead of quoting an isolated amount.
